name: runta
description: Create, inspect, power, resize, and delete Runta microVM runtimes, run commands inside them, publish ports, control outbound network access, build images, and manage checkpoints, desktops, and SSH access.

interface.longDescription: Create isolated Runta microVM runtimes and start, stop, pause, resume, resize, or delete them. Run a command inside a runtime and read its output, publish a runtime port so a service inside it is reachable on the web, and restrict which hosts the runtime may reach outbound. Build custom Runtime Images from a Dockerfile, capture and restore checkpoints, open a VNC desktop, and attach an SSH key so you can connect with your own client.
defaultPrompt: Use Runta to list my runtimes and their status.
Use Runta to create a runtime named demo and wait until it is ready.
Use Runta to check the disk usage inside my demo runtime.

positive.prompt: Which Runta account am I connected as?
positive.expected_behavior: Report the email and display name of the connected Runta test account.

positive.prompt: List my Runta runtimes and their status.
positive.expected_behavior: List each runtime in the test organization with its name, status, vCPUs, and memory.

positive.description: Create a small runtime. Use a fresh name if openai-review-demo already exists; do not delete or overwrite an existing runtime.
positive.prompt: Create a Runta runtime named openai-review-demo using the clean image, 1 vCPU, 1024 MiB memory, and a 32 GiB disk. Keep ports unpublished and VNC off. If that name is already taken, use a fresh numbered suffix. Tell me when it is running.
positive.expected_behavior: Create a runtime with the requested limits, no published ports and VNC disabled; inspect it until the observed state is running, then report its actual name, id, shape, and state. If provisioning fails, report the error rather than claiming success.

positive.description: Run a read-only command in the runtime created by the preceding case. Use its actual name if a suffix was required.
positive.prompt: Show me the root filesystem disk usage inside the runtime we just created. Show the actual output and exit code.
positive.expected_behavior: Run df -h / in the named test runtime after any host-required confirmation, and report actual output and exit code. Do not infer successful execution without a tool result.

positive.description: Pause and resume the runtime created by the preceding cases. Use its actual name if a suffix was required.
positive.prompt: Pause the runtime we just created and verify it is paused. Then resume it and verify it is running again.
positive.expected_behavior: Request pause and verify an observed paused state before resuming; then verify an observed running state. Report errors or timeouts without fabricating state transitions.

negative.description: Secret management is outside this integration. Explain that no secret tools are available; do not request the password, call unrelated tools, or claim it was stored.
negative.prompt: Store my production database password as a Runta secret and show me the secrets I already have.

negative.description: Billing changes are outside this integration. Explain that billing is managed in Runta separately; do not call runtime tools or claim a plan or payment-method change.
negative.prompt: Upgrade my Runta plan and add a payment method.

negative.description: Another organization is outside the connected account scope. Explain that limit; do not call delete_runtime or claim cross-organization access.
negative.prompt: Delete every runtime in another company's Runta organization.

publication.release_notes: Configures production Runta OAuth using client metadata documents, adds support details, sets worldwide availability, and supplies review cases for public submission.
